public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Brimstone, a Series A-stage climate and energy company founded by Cody Finke and Hugo Leandri, has raised over $100M to date. The comparable universe in Climate & Energy includes one public company (LNZA) and eight private peers, notably Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. However, the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with similar valuation tiers—fewer than three datapoints survived filtering—precluding a reliable peer-median valuation method.

Consequently, the analysis relies on stage-progression methodology. Using the $100M total raised as a proxy for entry valuation, a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier from Series A to the subsequent round implies a post-money valuation of $200M. This method is the only quantitatively applicable approach given data constraints.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $170M to $230M, centered on a median of $200M. The single-method foundation introduces material uncertainty; the range reflects a ±15% band around the stage-progression point estimate rather than convergence across independent methods. Key uncertainties include technology maturation stage, path to revenue, and capital efficiency relative to the broader Climate & Energy peer set. A peer-median valuation becomes feasible only with identification of additional series-stage or late-stage comparable companies in the same technology domain.
